name: DJ Vic
blurb: A touring act whose old site buried the booking and barely showed up in search. We rebuilt it around how clients actually choose — wedding, club, corporate — and took its search score from 38 to 92.

caseStudy.challenge: An in-demand international DJ with a site that buried the booking and barely registered in search. Enquiries were leaking to word-of-mouth and third parties instead of landing with him directly.
approach: Rebuilt on Astro around how clients actually choose — routed by event type: weddings, corporate, clubs.
Pulled his remixes and The Vic Fix series into the same journey, so the catalogue works for the booking.
Hardened the structure and schema for Google and AI search from the ground up.
Wired a 24-hour reply promise straight to WhatsApp and email.
caseStudy.outcome: The rebuild took the site's search score from 38 to 92, and every enquiry now arrives pre-routed to the right offer.

name: DJ Rhea
blurb: Her real edge — live darbuka played over the set — kept getting lost in a generic DJ pitch. We built her a site as premium as the rooms she plays, led with the live element, and made every enquiry arrive qualified.

caseStudy.challenge: A DJ whose real differentiator — live darbuka played over the set — was getting lost in a generic DJ pitch, in front of an audience that judges luxury in seconds.
approach: Built an ultra-luxury identity: towering serif display on gold and black.
Led with the live-percussion element, not the decks.
A booking flow that captures the date, the room and the brief before it ever reaches her inbox.
Astro and a Cloudflare Worker, with enquiries delivered by email through Cloudflare.
caseStudy.outcome: A site as premium as the rooms she plays, with every enquiry arriving qualified. Live now as phase one of a three-phase build.

name: Lloyd’s Pro Sound & Lighting
blurb: Eighteen years of reputation that lived only in word-of-mouth. We put the proof up front — 1,000+ events and a 4.7★ rating — and turned a WhatsApp thread into a site that does the booking.

caseStudy.challenge: Eighteen years of reputation that lived almost entirely in word-of-mouth and WhatsApp threads. Nothing online was doing the convincing, or the admin.
approach: Put the proof up front — 1,000+ events since 2008 and a 4.7★ rating.
Gave every event type its own page.
Made direct WhatsApp booking reachable from anywhere on the site.
Built a superadmin back office behind it: inventory and invoicing.
caseStudy.outcome: A site that does the selling and a back office that runs the quotes and the jobs. [Ask Lloyd for a result to quote.]

name: DJ Gags
blurb: Twenty-six years of credits scattered across socials and a press kit. We pulled them into one photography-led case, with the residencies and the résumé doing the convincing above the fold.

caseStudy.challenge: Twenty-six years of credits scattered across socials and a press kit, with no single place that made the case for a booking.
approach: A photography-led site where the images carry the room.
Framed twenty-six years and six residencies as proof, above the fold.
Put an availability check and WhatsApp booking in reach from the first screen.
caseStudy.outcome: One confident home for the booking, with the work and the résumé doing the convincing.

name: SNLA · Sapna Naik Landscape Architecture
blurb: A studio whose gardens sell themselves — if you can actually see them. We stripped the site back to the images and let the work carry the room, with everything else a quiet click away.

caseStudy.challenge: A landscape-architecture studio whose work is deeply visual, but whose old presence buried it under text and navigation.
approach: An image-first, full-bleed layout so the gardens speak before the words do.
Stripped navigation back to keep attention on the work.
Project stories, careers and contact always one click away.
caseStudy.outcome: A portfolio that lets the work carry the room. [Ask SNLA for a result to quote.]

name: Supriya Bopanna
blurb: Choosing a therapist is a trust decision, and most practice sites read clinical. We built a calm, branded home — a custom “Perspective” identity and plain language — that makes the first message easier to send.

caseStudy.challenge: Choosing a therapist is a trust decision, and most practice sites read clinical or templated — a quiet barrier to that first message.
approach: A custom “Perspective” wordmark and calm, editorial design.
Plain-language explanation of how sessions work and who the practice is for.
A private, considered contact flow.
A separate admin back office: content editing, a client CRM and no-GST invoicing.
caseStudy.outcome: A calm home that makes the first message easier to send. Live on the apex and www.

name: Bengaluru DJs Collective
blurb: A scene where everyone books the nights but no one’s in the same room. We built it a home rather than a storefront — no headliner, no hard sell, just a confident way to belong and keep up.

caseStudy.challenge: A city full of people who book the nights but never meet — a community to build, not a product to sell.
approach: Positioned it as a home for the scene, not a storefront — no headliner, no hard sell.
A bold gold-on-black identity with real attitude.
Recaps of past editions and a simple, clear way in.
Its own repo, deployed on Cloudflare Pages.
caseStudy.outcome: A confident place to belong and keep up, live on bengalurudjscollective.com.

name: Flingit
blurb: Anyone can sell a bottle; the hard part is selling a night. We built the world around the drink — a bilingual, gamified platform that turns 230+ stockists into somewhere to actually go.

caseStudy.challenge: Anyone can sell a bottle; the hard part is selling a night. Flingit needed a world, not a product page.
approach: A moody, bilingual (English / Kannada) experience.
A spot-finder across 230+ stockists.
Gamified play: events, rewards and a weekly leaderboard.
A proper age gate up front.
caseStudy.outcome: A platform that turns 230+ stockists into somewhere to actually go. [Ask Flingit for a result to quote.]
